title: runtime/kv: eviction policy v1 (victim selection + fairness constraints) + simulator tests
author: Lena Fischer
release_notes:
- Add eviction policy v1 for KV cache blocks with fairness constraints and scheduler-aware priority classes.
- Add simulator-based tests covering starvation/fairness and pathological fragmentation scenarios.
description:
Context

KV cache fragmentation under bursty traffic causes allocation churn and tail latency spikes (see PM-2025-02-11, SUP-4391). As part of the KV compaction project, we need an explicit eviction policy that (a) produces stable allocation behavior under pressure and (b) does not starve tenants / priority classes.

This PR implements eviction policy v1 (victim selection + fairness constraints) and adds a lightweight simulator test harness to exercise the policy under mixed workloads.

What this PR does

- Introduces EvictionPolicyV1, operating on KV “blocks” (allocator abstraction introduced in PR-18431).
- Defines explicit priority classes for eviction eligibility and ordering:
  - P0: system/infra reserved (never evict)
  - P1: pinned / in-flight decode protected (never evict)
  - P2: active sequences (eligible only under "hard" pressure; guarded by min-residency)
  - P3: prefix-cache / reusable segments (eligible; weighted by reuse score)
  - P4: completed / cold segments (eligible; preferred)
- Victim scoring combines: age (LRU-ish), tenant fairness debt, SLA tier, and reuse score (for prefix cache segments) with guardrails:
  - Min-residency window to avoid thrash immediately after allocation
  - Per-tenant eviction budget (token-equivalent) to prevent one tenant from getting repeatedly evicted under global pressure
  - “No starvation” invariant: if a tenant remains in the runnable set and is eligible for eviction, it must receive eviction service within a bounded number of global evictions (implemented via deficit round-robin over tenants)
- Exposes structured eviction reasons + counters for observability (reason labels only; metrics plumbing lands separately in PR-18423).
- Adds simulator tests that model:
  - Bursty arrivals with mixed context lengths (prefill/decode interleaving)
  - Multi-tenant pools with tiered SLAs
  - Prefix-cache heavy workloads (high reuse) vs no-reuse
  - Pathological patterns that previously caused eviction ping-pong

Non-goals / intentionally not in this PR

- Compaction / block moving logic (PR-18457)
- Scheduler contract changes / cache pressure signals (PR-18463)
- Final trigger/budget policy (ADR-0128)

Design notes

This policy is aligned with ADR-0129 (eviction policy + scheduler contract): the policy is deterministic given an allocator snapshot + scheduler-provided per-request metadata (tenant_id, priority_class, min_residency_deadline, reuse_score). In this PR the scheduler metadata is wired via a thin adapter and defaults are used where the scheduler does not yet provide the fields.

Key API surfaces:

- runtime/kv/eviction/eviction_policy.h
  - SelectVictims(requested_blocks, snapshot, constraints) -> VictimSet
- runtime/kv/eviction/fairness.h
  - DeficitRoundRobinTenantArbiter

Correctness / safety

- Never evict blocks that are marked as in-flight by the runtime (allocator snapshot carries in_flight=true).
- Min-residency enforced by comparing now() with block.allocated_at.
- Under “hard pressure” mode, policy may return victims from active sequences but only if (a) they are beyond min-residency and (b) the tenant has exceeded its soft budget; simulator validates bounded impact.

Testing

- Added simulator-based tests under runtime/kv/eviction/sim/.
- New unit tests validate:
  - no-evict classes (P0/P1) are never chosen
  - fairness: tenant eviction share converges to configured weights within tolerance
  - no-starvation: upper bound on the number of global evictions before each eligible tenant is served
  - reuse-aware behavior: high reuse_score blocks are evicted later than cold blocks

Performance

The policy runs on allocator snapshot metadata (CPU) and is intended to be O(n log n) with bounded constants (n = candidate blocks). We cap candidates by taking a prefiltered list from the allocator (eligible sets by class) and limiting to max_candidates_per_round (default 4096). Simulator shows <1ms per decision on typical candidate sizes. (Real runtime profiling will be validated once compaction triggers are integrated.)

Rollout

- Feature gated by runtime flag: kv_eviction_policy=v1 (default remains legacy)
- Canary plan and metrics gating tracked in ENG-2851/ENG-2852 (not in this PR)

Follow-ups

- Wire scheduler-provided reuse score from prefix-cache heuristics (ENG-2855)
- Integrate cache pressure signal & overload behavior (PR-18463)
- Tune weights using perf suite burst scenarios (ENG-2843)

Checklist

- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Simulator tests added
- [x] Docs in code comments for scoring terms
- [x] No change to default behavior (flagged)

Refs: ENG-2845, ADR-0129, PM-2025-02-11, SUP-4391
commits: kv/eviction: introduce EvictionPolicyV1 interface and default configuration
kv/eviction: implement victim scoring (age, fairness debt, tier, reuse)
kv/eviction: add tenant fairness arbiter (deficit round-robin) + invariants
kv/eviction: add min-residency guardrails and hard-pressure fallback
kv/eviction/sim: add simulator harness and baseline scenarios
kv/eviction/tests: add fairness + no-starvation + reuse-aware unit tests
runtime flags: add kv_eviction_policy=v1 and config parsing
conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): Can you spell out the exact no-starvation guarantee? The ADR text says “bounded number of global evictions” but we need to be precise for scheduler integration.

Lena Fischer (author): Added a comment + test asserting: for N eligible tenants with positive demand and weights w_i, each tenant i must be selected within <= ceil((sum_w / w_i) * K) global evictions (K = 2 right now). The simulator test enforces this bound with randomized workloads. Happy to adjust K if you prefer a tighter/looser bound.
Omar El-Sayed (review): Please confirm we never evict anything marked in_flight. With compaction coming, in_flight will be conservative and we cannot take risks here.

Lena Fischer (author): Confirmed. Snapshot candidates are filtered by in_flight=false and class != P0/P1. Added an explicit ASSERT in SelectVictims() and a unit test that injects an in_flight candidate to ensure it is ignored.

Grace Kim (review): Concerned about the hard-pressure path touching active sequences. Are we sure min-residency is sufficient to avoid evict/realloc ping-pong in decode? Also, how do we coordinate with stream sync?

Lena Fischer (author): Hard-pressure path is off by default (kv_eviction_hard_pressure=false) and only intended for “allocator failure” fallback. In this PR it just returns a victim set; the actual safe free/move will still go through allocator + stream synchronization (PR-18457/18463). I added stronger guards: min-residency + tenant soft budget exceeded + only from P2 if P3/P4 insufficient.
Marcus Reed (review): Can you add at least one simulator scenario that mimics the perf suite’s bursty-mix distribution? We want to compare policy changes over time.

Lena Fischer (author): Added scenarios/bursty_mix_test.cc with the same arrival distribution and length buckets we use in the perf harness. It outputs a compact summary (evictions/sec, fairness error, mean decision time) for future baselining.
Noah Patel (review): Naming: "reuse_score" should be defined more clearly. Is higher == more reusable? Also, can we keep scoring coefficients in config, not hard-coded?

Lena Fischer (author): Clarified: reuse_score is [0,1], higher means more likely reused, therefore *less* likely to be evicted (we subtract it in the score). Coefficients moved into EvictionPolicyV1Config and are wired to runtime config parsing (still behind flag).

Sofia Ivanova (review): Requested change: please ensure tenant fairness is applied after eligibility filtering but before priority-class sorting; otherwise P3/P4 skew can starve P2 under sustained load.

Lena Fischer (author): Updated ordering: we select a tenant via DRR first, then pick the best victim within that tenant’s eligible candidates using priority class + score. Added test that ensures eligible P2 work isn’t starved when P4 is constantly replenished by another tenant.
Buildkite (bot): buildkite/redwood-runtime-sim-tests failed (timeout in randomized fairness test, seed=18444-27).
Lena Fischer (author): Reduced randomized scenario length and added deterministic regression case; also fixed an O(n^2) loop in the simulator stats collector that was dominating runtime.
Buildkite (bot): All checks passed.
Omar El-Sayed (review): LGTM after the in_flight asserts and config move. Please make sure the flag default remains legacy.
Lena Fischer (author): Confirmed: default kv_eviction_policy=legacy. v1 only when explicitly enabled.
Sofia Ivanova (review): Approved. This matches the contract direction for ADR-0129; we’ll hook in scheduler metadata in 18463.
Connor O'Brien (comment): Merging via squash to keep release branch cherry-picks clean. Please coordinate if you need a backport for the canary build.
Lena Fischer (author): Sounds good.
